To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tuf sequence of several phytoplasmas is highly conserved among phytoplasmas but not with other mollicute sequences and that it is a suitable gene for phytoplasma identification and classification.

the tuf-gene is a useful phylogenetic marker for the differentiation and classification of aster yellows, X-disease and stolbur group phytoplasmas, and that the tuf genes are present as a single-copy in the genomes of these phytoplasmas.
the tuf genes of several phytoplasmas have been sequenced and used to develop primers and probes for the differentiation of phytoplasma taxa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new molecular tool for phylogenetic studies on phytoplasmas, the aster yellows group in particular.
the use of a phylogenetic marker for phytoplasma differentiation and classification.
the use of the tuf genes of phytoplasma for the development of a new molecular method of phytoplasmal differentiation and classification, and for studying phytoplasma genome organization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tuf genes of all the phytoplasmal species examined in this study have a high degree of sequence conservation, which is reflected by a high degree of similarity in the deduced amino acids.
the tuf genes of the phytoplamsas are highly conserved in their primary structure, but the tuf gene of phytoplasma is highly variable at the nucleotide level.

the tuf genes of the phytoplasmatales are more conserved than the 16S rDNA, but less conserved than the ribosomal protein genes, and thus can be used to differentiate between the phytoplasms and to classify them into phylogenetic groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tuf genes from different phytoplasmas are highly conserved, but the nucleotide sequences are variable enough for differentiation and classification of the phytoplasmic strains by RFLP.
tuf gene has potential to be used for phylogenetic analysis, classification and detection of phytoplasma species.
the tuf sequence can be used to differentiate the phytoplasmal strains and that the tuf sequences are conserved enough to be used to classify phytoplasma species.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tuf genes of phytoplasma are useful for differentiation and classification of the phytoplasmal groups and the phytoplasms can be differentiated into subgroups based on the RFLP patterns of their tuf genes.
we have developed a molecular tool for the detection and differentiation of phytoplasma species.
the EF-Tu gene is a good candidate gene for phytoplasma identification, and that it can be used for phytoplasmal differentiation.
